llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated ARI mobile-listing purpose, but it needs review because its supposedly fixed workflow can be overridden to run broader paid product-operation workflows.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTPS requests are fixed to https://ari.funewa.com with redirect blocking and are disclosed in the docs. The transmitted data includes ASIN/site/product-operation requests and account-linked API calls, which is expected for the service but sensitive enough for user awareness.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, dependency installation, remote code retrieval, or tool replacement was found. The skill grants Bash access to run the bundled Python CLI, which stores an ARI API key in the user's home config when setup/configure is used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly say not to switch workflows or accept arbitrary prompts, but the CLI exposes workflow/focus override arguments and validates them only against remote account capabilities, not against this skill's fixed scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The only persistence found is the ARI API key saved to ~/.ari/config.json with 0600 permissions where supported. No background services, scheduled jobs, shell profile edits, destructive file operations, or local privilege escalation behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is fixed Amazon mobile Listing diagnosis using listing/mobile, and setup, configure, check, collect, status, and ARI API use are disclosed and broadly purpose-aligned. However, operations quote/run accept caller-supplied --workflow and --focus values that override the packaged listing/mobile defaults, allowing any server-enabled product-operation workflow for the account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you rely on the package to enforce only mobile Listing optimization. Use it only with an ARI account and credits you are willing to use, verify any quoted workflow/request before confirming, and avoid passing --workflow or --focus overrides unless you intentionally want broader ARI product-operation behavior.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted. The auxiliary authorization, balance, collection, and status commands are disclosed and coherent, but the broader operations workflow override exceeds the advertised fixed mobile-listing boundary.
[LP1] expected: Downgraded in isolation. Network use to the ARI service is disclosed and constrained to the official domain; it becomes relevant mainly because the operation scope can be widened by workflow/focus overrides.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the operations surface. The artifact exposes generic workflow/focus parameters inside an allowed operations command despite the specialized package claiming a fixed listing/mobile contract.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted. The code uses caller-supplied workflow/focus before packaged defaults and approves any combination returned by the server capabilities endpoint.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted. The comments and docs describe immutable specialized defaults, but the runtime implementation still permits workflow/focus overrides.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a medium least-privilege concern. This does not bypass ARI account authorization or the explicit --confirm requirement, but it does bypass the narrower capability boundary promised by this package.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded. The changelog discusses removal of autoconfirm behavior, and current collect/run paths require quote-first behavior plus explicit --confirm before paid execution.
[SQP-3] expected: Not treated as a security concern for this verdict. The artifacts are Chinese-language and hard-code /zh links, but this does not show hidden behavior, unsafe authority, or malicious action.
[P9] expected: Downgraded. The blank-line padding is present, but manual inspection around the flagged regions showed spacing between functions, not hidden instructions or payloads.
[AST7] expected: Downgraded. The dynamic getattr use is limited to known argparse attribute names for ASIN normalization and does not create arbitrary code execution or privilege expansion.
